repo_standards_ref: references/global-crew.md (minimal change / no speculative abstraction / fail-visibly / match surrounding conventions), references/global-everyone.md

smells.finding: Low-severity, non-blocking: the resolver's token-family knowledge is expressed across THREE regexes (_ROLE_SKILL_DIR_RE, _ROLE_SESSION_ID_RE for discovery; _RESOLVER_OWNED_TOKEN_RE for the assertion). Adding a fourth token family means editing both the discovery pair and the assertion regex, which must stay in sync. Acceptable as-is (each serves a distinct purpose and reads clearly), but noted so a future family-add keeps them aligned.

override.repo_standard: references/global-crew.md: 'Make the minimal change that satisfies the handoff; no speculative abstraction.'
override.reason: The (launch_order, ownership, return_shape) trio travels main()->stage_feedback()->_fence_text(), a candidate for a FenceSpec object. Introducing a param object for three fields used along one call chain is the speculative abstraction the minimal-change standard subordinates; the fields also map 1:1 to distinct CLI flags.

smells.finding: Low-severity, non-blocking: stage_feedback() takes ~11 params (root, work_id + 9 keyword-only). Real, but mitigated: all optional params are keyword-only with sane defaults and each maps 1:1 to a CLI flag with a single call site. Worth a config/dataclass only if this grows; not worth churning the minimal fix now.

override.repo_standard: Issue #114/#154 handoff intent: prevent recurrence of the unresolved-placeholder defect for a NEW role's token, not just the one token in front of us.
override.reason: Pattern-based token discovery (vs hardcoding a second role) plus hyphenated-role handling could read as speculative, but the handoff explicitly scopes the fix to the defect CLASS so a third role cannot recur it under a fresh token. That makes the generalization sanctioned scope, not speculation; it is also the minimal general fix for the real admiral bug.
